headline: FORTY-ONE PERCENT OF AMERICANS NOW PAY MONEY TO AVOID ADVERTISING.  SIX PERCENT RUN AN AD BLOCKER.  THE AGENCY THAT PUBLISHED THAT ON MONDAY ANNOUNCED THE PRODUCT THAT ANSWERS IT ON TUESDAY
deck: Omnicom Media Intelligence surveyed 1,136 US adults and ran a separate 1,200-person behavioural study.  The figure everybody will quote is 65 percent.  The figure that changes a media plan is 41 against 6.
tldr: Omnicom Media Intelligence surveyed 1,136 US adults and found that 41 percent pay for subscriptions to avoid advertising while only 6 percent actively block ads, and that 79 percent remember a brand better from sponsored content they enjoyed than from a traditional commercial.  Ask your agency for the paid ad-free share of your target audience on every platform you buy, and write that number into the plan even when it is an estimate.

Omnicom announced an in-content placement partnership with Rembrand a day after that research, claiming 5.5 times the message recall and 4 times the purchase intent, but only when the placement runs alongside a conventional video ad in the same show.  Write that pairing into your next branded content plan, put the placement and the ad inside the same programme, and ask any vendor for the placement result without a paired ad before you agree a price.

Dhar Mann pledged to broker 100 million dollars of creator and brand deals at Advertising Week, will not name a single chief marketing officer, and says himself that budgets set months ago will not suddenly open, while top creators told him they did not know how to pitch a brand.  Write a one-page pitch with dated numbers for every creator you work with this week, and ask for that page before your next meeting if you sit on the brand side.

The quarter's biggest hours-watched figure in esports, LCK's 70,984,814, came from a league that ran for months and placed only sixth on peak viewers at 1,556,100, while the LCS summer final set a four-year peak record as the channels carrying it rose from 100 to 126.  Ask for peak concurrents, average concurrents, hours watched, airtime and channel count on one page for every live proposal, and set the rate against average concurrents.

YouTube and Google.org put 2.5 million dollars into Mark Rober's free Class CrunchLabs curriculum, which is the top of his paid science kit business, and the step that makes it travel is that the lessons are aligned to a teaching standard so a teacher can drop them into a unit plan.  Make the good version of whatever your audience already pays for badly, give it away in the format they actually use, and align it to the standard they are measured against.

Planes, Trains, Everything., 156,000 subscribers, does roughly double the views on videos about a bookable vehicle than on destination guides, and its biggest video of the quarter, at 243,628 views, asks whether one named ferry lounge upgrade is worth the money, for a company that has never paid him.  Commission an honest review of your own upgrade decision from a channel whose audience is already pricing it, and put a tracked booking link underneath.

Twitch launched a Shopping category on its homepage before Prime Day and filled it largely with Amazon Live sellers rather than Twitch streamers, and the streams reportedly are not finding views.  Ask who is hosting the stream and how long that person's audience has existed on that platform before agreeing a rate on any new shopping placement, and price an imported host like a banner rather than a creator deal.
